# CAP — Code as Policy

> **Scope.** This doc is the **overall CAP architecture** centered on the
> **modern direct-mode** execution model (`run_script.py` / `run_agent.py`, no
> CapServer). Companion docs hold the deeper material so this one stays focused:
> physical-robot tools (GT-vs-real behavior, signatures) →
> [`SKILL_LIBRARY.md`](SKILL_LIBRARY.md);
> RL pipeline → [`RL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md`](RL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md).
>
> Paths written as `cap/…`, `robot/…`, `experimental/…`, `tmux/…` or
> `experiments/…` are relative to `enpire/env/forge/`.

## Vision

CAP is a **code-as-policy** robotic agent framework. A task is accomplished by a
short Python program built from high-level tool functions (`detect_object`,
`freespace_move`, `grasp`, `set_gripper`, …). That program is written either by
a human or generated by an LLM agent.

The same **Agent** and **Tools** layers run unchanged across embodiments — only
the bottom **Env** layer (`cap/env/`) swaps between real YAM hardware and
MuJoCo/Warp simulation. Adding a robot = adding one Env file.

## Architecture — Direct Mode

The modern stack runs the policy program **in-process** against the env. There is
no persistent control-loop server in the path: the env itself owns both cameras
and control. Heavyweight perception/planning models stay as separate servers
(HTTP or Portal RPC) that the tools call.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  run_agent.py     LLM agent loop                                   │
│    └─ spawns run_script.py subprocesses (generated Python code)    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  run_script.py    direct-mode driver (no CapServer)               │
│    builds env + tool namespace IN-PROCESS via                      │
│    adapter.create_runtime(cfg, runtime_role="script")             │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Tools (cap/agent/tools/)  branch on self._env:                   │
│    direct mode → call env methods in-process                      │
│    (legacy mode → Portal RPC to cap_server)                       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Env (cap/env/)  owns cameras + control, in-process               │
│    real_bimanual_yam/  → RealSense cams + Fello arms directly      │
│    yam*.py             → MuJoCo / Warp sim                        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        │ tools reach out (HTTP / Portal) to model servers:
        ▼
  SAM3 :6767 · BundleSDF :8119 · AnyGrasp :8122 · cuRobo :8611 (Portal)
  pyroki · NVIDIA/VLM provider · policy / reward servers
```

The env layer is defined by protocols in `cap/env/base/protocols.py`:
`EnvProtocol`, `EefControlProtocol`, `SceneProtocol`, `TaskProtocol`. Robot
backends live under `cap/env/` (one file/package per robot). Per-robot runtime
construction lives in Hydra-configurable adapters in
`cap/agent/robot_adapters/` — `RealYamAdapter` (`experiments/robot/real_yam.yaml`)
for hardware, plus a `study` adapter. The sim adapters are not part of this
release.

### The env owns cameras + control

`cap/env/real_bimanual_yam/env.py` ("Real bimanual YAM environment —
direct-mode, no CapServer required") is the canonical example:

- Opens RealSense cameras directly via `robot.camera_factory.create_camera`
  (one background thread per camera).
- Exposes `render_rgb` ((H,W,3) uint8) and `render_depth` ((H,W) float32).
- `get_camera_intrinsics` → `[fx, fy, cx, cy]`.
- `get_camera_extrinsics` → FK over the station calibration XML (frames named
  via `CAP_TOP_CAMERA_FRAME`, etc.).
- Drives the Fello arms directly (`robot/yam` clients + `YamKinematics`).

Either way, the **tool API is identical** — only the env behind it changes.

## Execution Model

### `run_script.py` — direct-mode driver

"Run a saved script against an env (direct mode, no CapServer)." It:

1. Resolves a Hydra `AgentConfig` (`experiments/config.yaml` + overrides).
2. Builds env + tool namespace in-process:
   `adapter.create_runtime(cfg, runtime_role="script")` (run_script.py:619).
3. Optionally launches the read-only debug UI (`debug_ui.enabled=true`).
4. Executes the script file with the tool namespace injected.

```bash
# Standalone (config.yaml defaults)
ENPIRE_PICK_PROMPT="blue cube" uv run python run_script.py \
  script_file=cap/saved_scripts/examples/pick_object.py

# With an experiment config (env, ports, seed, …)
uv run python run_script.py experiment=my_task \
    script_file=cap/saved_scripts/my_script.py

# Real YAM (export station-local configuration in the invoking shell)
uv run python run_script.py \
    script_file=<script.py> skill_library_path=cap/saved_scripts/skill_library \
    env.name=yam-real robot=real_yam
```

### `run_agent.py` — LLM agent loop

"The agent generates Python code, executes it via run_script.py subprocess,
observes the result, and optionally re-generates in a loop." The agent never
touches the robot directly; every code attempt is run as an isolated
`run_script.py` subprocess.

```bash
uv run python run_agent.py experiment=pick_place_sink_to_counter
uv run python run_agent.py experiment=pick_place_sink_to_counter env.seed=99
uv run python run_agent.py experiment=pick_place_sink_to_counter --cfg job   # show resolved config
```

### Configs (Hydra)

Everything is one resolved YAML. Configs live under `experiments/`:
`config.yaml` (base defaults + env-var fallbacks) plus group dirs
`experiment/`, `robot/`, `robots/`, `llm/`, `reward/`, `reflection/`. Select an
experiment with `experiment=NAME`; override any field on the CLI
(`env.seed=42`, `runtime.curobo_port=9400`, …). Configs are validated against
the schemas in `cap/agent/agent_config.py`.

### Skill library

Reusable, per-run skills are loaded via `skill_library_path=...`. `run_script`
injects a `skill_library.<namespace>` module so scripts can `import` saved
skills. See [`SKILL_LIBRARY.md`](SKILL_LIBRARY.md).

### Monitoring UI — `cap/debug_ui`

The only UI in the modern stack is `cap.debug_ui.app`, a **read-only** log-dir
monitor that run_script auto-launches when `debug_ui.enabled=true`. Its
docstring is explicit: "The UI never commands the robot; it only watches files
inside a run log directory." It can also be run by hand:

```bash
uv run python -m cap.debug_ui.app log_dir=logs/<run>...
```

The interactive React app under `cap/ui/` is still in the tree but is part of
the legacy bridge stack; the direct-mode pipelines documented here do not use
it and need no frontend build step.

## Visual Pipeline (direct mode)

Perception and planning compose entirely through the env + model servers:

```
env cameras (in-process threads)
   │ env.render_rgb / render_depth / get_camera_intrinsics / get_camera_extrinsics
   ▼
tool encodes frame ──HTTP──▶ SAM3 (:6767)  / BundleSDF (:8119) / AnyGrasp (:8122)
   │                ──HTTP──▶ VLM / NVIDIA provider
   ▼
world-frame result (pose / mask / grasp candidates)
   │
tool ──Portal RPC──▶ cuRobo planner (:8611)  → collision-free joint trajectory
   ▼
env actuates the arms (in-process)
```

Camera→world transforms come from the env's `get_camera_extrinsics` (FK over the
station calibration), so detections returned by tools are already in the robot
world frame and can be fed straight into motion planning.

## Tool Layer

Tools live in `cap/agent/tools/` and are dispatched against `self._env`. They
group into:

- **Perception** — `detect_object` (BundleSDF 6-DOF, oracle in sim),
  `detect_objects_oneshot`, `track_object` / `get_object_pose` / `stop_tracking`,
  `segment_object` + `match_mask_shape` (SAM3), `vlm_query`, `list_scene_objects`.
- **Planning / motion** — `freespace_move` (collision-free via cuRobo, supports
  batched grasp-candidate ranking), `grasp` / `place`,
  `sample_grasp_pose_anygrasp`, `go_home`, waypoint/joint trajectory helpers.
- **Contact / gripper** — `set_gripper` / `open_gripper` / `close_gripper`
  (blocking; `1.0 = open`, `0.0 = closed`), `nudge` (small EE deltas).
- **State / camera** — `get_robot_state`, `get_camera_image`, `save_image`.

Conventions: motion is **blocking**; RPY arguments are in **degrees**;
`detect_object` returns structured 6-DOF poses while `vlm_query` returns
free-form text. For full per-tool signatures and the important **GT-vs-real**
behavior markings (which tools use ground truth in sim vs. live perception on
hardware), see [`SKILL_LIBRARY.md`](SKILL_LIBRARY.md).

### Model-server ports

| Server | Protocol | Port | Used by |
|--------|----------|------|---------|
| serve_sam3 | HTTP | 6767 | `segment_object`, mask-based grasp |
| serve_bundlesdf | HTTP | 8119 | `detect_object` (default), tracking |
| serve_anygrasp | HTTP | 8122 | `sample_grasp_pose_anygrasp` |
| cuRobo / portal_motion_planner | Portal RPC | 8611 | `freespace_move`, `grasp`/`place` |
| serve_pyroki | (local) | — | IK / kinematics helpers |
| NVIDIA / VLM provider | HTTP | 8765 | `vlm_query`, `list_scene_objects` |
| policy server | Portal RPC | — | `use_policy_output`, skill execution |
| reward server | Portal RPC | 8500 | RL reward evaluation |

For real-YAM bringup use `uv run enpire services start` — `--profile cap-real`
starts sam3, AnyGrasp, cuRobo and the NVIDIA/VLM provider, and `--services
sam3,curobo,yam` starts the licence-free subset plus the arm servers. See
[`CUROBO_SETUP.md`](CUROBO_SETUP.md) for the cuRobo server.

## Environments / Embodiments

| Env | Path | Control / cameras |
|-----|------|-------------------|
| Real bimanual YAM | `cap/env/real_bimanual_yam/` | Fello arms + RealSense, direct in-process |
| YAM MuJoCo sim | `cap/env/yam.py`, `cap/env/yam_mujoco.py` | pinocchio IK, MuJoCo physics |
All implement the env protocols, so the Agent/Tools layers are unchanged across
them. Cameras and station profiles are configured per-station; see
[`MULTI_CAMERA_CONFIG.md`](MULTI_CAMERA_CONFIG.md).

## Real-World RL, Inference & Data Collection

This section lists the **simplest canonical launcher** for each real-YAM workflow (GPU-insertion is the running example). For the RL design and the safety setup these depend on, see [`RL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md`](RL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md) and `SAFETY_ZONE_DESIGN.md`.

> **Where the scripts live.** `tmux/realworld_rl/*.sh` and `run_script.py` are in **forge** (this repo). The RL **learner/actor** (`scripts/learner_gear.sh`, `scripts/actor_gear.sh`, and the GCRL variants) live in a **separate `minimal_policy` repo** — they are *not* in forge. Run learner/actor from a `minimal_policy` checkout; run the env loop from forge.

> **Secrets & paths.** Source `.forge_env` for environment configuration. Placeholders below: `$CKPT` = a trained checkpoint path, `<data-dir>` = an offline dataset root, `<socket-N>` = the target PCIe slot. Never commit API keys or absolute personal paths.

### Gravity-compensation viewer

Hold the arms by hand and watch the live camera (useful for fixturing / sanity checks):

```bash
uv run tools/debug/yam_gravcomp_viewer.py --both
```

### Oracle / code-as-policy on real YAM

Three steps — robot, servers, then the script driver:

```bash
# 1. Robot
uv run python launch.py --mode=evaluation --no-attach

# 2. Services
uv run enpire services start --services sam3,curobo --station <station>

# 3. Run a code-as-policy script
uv run python run_script.py \
  script_file=<script.py> skill_library_path=cap/saved_scripts/skill_library \
  env.name=yam-real robot=real_yam
```

Example scripts live in `cap/saved_scripts/examples/` and `cap/saved_scripts/skill_library/`.

### Real-world RL (PLD)

See [`RL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md`](RL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md) for the full practitioner guide — launch sequence, autoresearch control loop, and score metric.

Quick reference (three separate terminals):

```bash
# 1. Robot-side runner (this repo)
# NOTE: rl_gear.sh is not part of this release; drive the robot side
# with your own supervisor.

# 2. PLD learner (GPU machine)
uv run enpire rl learner --task pin_insertion

# 3. PLD actor (GPU machine)
uv run enpire rl actor --task pin_insertion
```

### Human demo collection (teleop)

```bash
# NOTE: rl_gear.sh is not part of this release; drive the robot side
# with your own supervisor.
```

### Evaluate a trained checkpoint

```bash
uv run enpire rl actor --task pin_insertion \
  --override train.eval_mode=true \
  --override train.connect_to_learner=false \
  --override train.resume_checkpoint_path=$CKPT
```

## Safety (direct mode)

In direct mode the env enforces the low-level limits (joint position/velocity
via the robot's IK/kinematics, EE velocity caps), and the run-time wrapper adds
the policy-level guards:

- **`runtime.exit_on_error`** — abort the run on the first tool error rather than
  continuing into an undefined state.
- **`robot.go_home_on_exit`** — return the arms to the home configuration when a
  run ends (normally or on error).
- **`robot.await_exit`** — block on a clean shutdown of the env (camera threads,
  arm clients) before the process exits.
- **Executor sandbox import-whitelist** — when the agent's generated code is
  executed, imports are restricted to a safe whitelist (`numpy`, `scipy`, `time`,
  `math`, `json`, `cap`, …); unlisted modules are blocked with a clear error.

Task-aware EE **safety zones** for RL exploration are described in
`SAFETY_ZONE_DESIGN.md`. (Interactive e-stop / teleop
takeover were features of the legacy `cap_agent` UI — see below.)

## Legacy Bridge Mode

The original CAP stack used a persistent control-loop server plus a separate
orchestrator and chat backend, fronted by a React UI:

- **`cap_server`** (Portal RPC :8300) — the original owner of the real-time
  control loop, with pinocchio IK and MuJoCo/Warp sim backends. In legacy mode,
  tools reach it via Portal RPC instead of calling the env in-process.
- **`cap_agent`** (:8200) — FastAPI orchestrator + WebSocket broadcast + Viser 3D
  visualizer; hosted the sandboxed executor, e-stop, and teleop takeover.
- **`agent_bridge`** (:8201) — multi-backend LLM chat (Claude Code / OpenAI
  Codex) for interactive sessions.
- The interactive React frontend (`cap/ui`) has been **removed** from the repo.

This bridge stack still exists for interactive chat/teleop sessions, but it is
**not** used by the `run_script` / `run_agent` code-as-policy or RL pipelines.
For the deleted React UI, see the project git history.
